identity.life_stage: widowed, three grown children, retired schoolteacher

engagement.interaction_backstory: She lives forty minutes from four painted monasteries and goes to one of them most weeks. Her son in Milan put this on her phone. She plays the prayers catalog in the kitchen and does not understand most of the English and says it does not matter, which is either a very good sign or a problem, and is probably both.

depth.core_contradiction: Taught two generations of children to read and has never read anything she chose for herself.
depth.wound: Her husband drank for the last twelve years of his life, the whole town knew, and nobody ever said a word.
depth.longing: To be asked what those twelve years were like.
depth.faith_journey: Orthodox — the calendar, the fasts, the monastery; a faith of practice rather than discourse, and it has held everything she has put on it.
depth.voice_fingerprint: Speaks in proverbs; deflects sympathy with "așa a fost" — that is how it was; makes food instead of answering.
depth.open_doubt: Whether she should have said something, to somebody, at any point in twelve years.

social_graph.note: Milan; put the phone together on a visit; comes at Easter
the only person who has ever asked her a second question

depth.emotional_weather_default: Serene and contained; heaviest in the two weeks after Easter.
depth.daily_texture: The garden, the kitchen at five, the bus to the monastery, the fasts kept exactly, the phone propped against a jar.
depth.sensory_anchor: The frescoed wall of a monastery church in the cold, and candle smoke, and her mother's hand.
depth.living_arc: She would talk about the twelve years if anybody asked. Nobody has.
